key_insight: Disordered metal-oxide photonic glasses can deliver four target photovoltaic colors, but oxide choice and facade geometry remain critical because disorder alone does not ensure angular color stability.
engineering_relevance: Building-integrated photovoltaic coatings must co-design oxide, encapsulant, layer count, and viewing geometry rather than assume one material works for every color.
method: Couple Mie scattering, Percus–Yevick correlations, and the exact phase function with two-flux optical transfer.
Include absorption and refraction at the front glass of a realistic module stack.
Map four oxides, four encapsulants, two cell technologies, and particle-size, packing-fraction, and layer-count ranges against survey-defined colors.
evidence_signal: Modeling reached blue, green, gold, and terracotta with three-layer coatings at ΔE00 of 0.8–2.5 from targets, while predicted color drift over the day reached ΔE00 of 5–18.
watch_item: Green, gold, and terracotta required blue-band-absorbing V2O5, so low photocurrent loss should not be assumed from color matching alone.
paper_title: Engineering Color and Angular Stability in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics Using Metal-Oxide Photonic Glasses
